ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows a hexagram made up of equilateral triangles, with a gray shaded hexagon in the center. The outer boundary of the star shape is composed of 12 identical small line segments, each line segment corresponding to the side of a small equilateral triangle; the shaded hexagon has 6 sides, each of which is also the same as the side length of these small equilateral triangles. Reasoning: Let the side length of each small equilateral triangle be s. The perimeter of the star shape is 36 cm, and the outer boundary has a total of 12 sides of length s, so 12s = 36, obtaining s = 3 cm. The shaded hexagon has 6 sides, each 3 cm long, so its perimeter is 6 × 3 = 18 cm.

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: the image shows a six-point star made on a triangular grid, with a shaded central hexagon. The outer boundary of the star consists of 12 congruent small line segments, each the side of one of the identical equilateral triangles. From the text, the star perimeter is 36 cm. Let each small triangle side be s. Then 12s = 36, so s = 3 cm. The shaded hexagon in the image has 6 sides, each also one small triangle side, so its perimeter is 6s = 18 cm.

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: the shaded region is a central hexagon, and each side of this hexagon has an unshaded equilateral triangle attached outward, forming the six points of the star. For each side of the shaded hexagon of length s, the attached equilateral triangle contributes two exposed outer sides to the star perimeter, each also length s. Thus, for every 1 side-length on the hexagon perimeter, there are 2 corresponding side-lengths on the star perimeter. Therefore the star perimeter is twice the shaded hexagon perimeter. Since the text gives the star perimeter as 36 cm, the shaded hexagon perimeter is 36 ÷ 2 = 18 cm.
